newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-C-C Amatil shares continue to fall.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-C-C Amatil shares continue to fall.

text.p: Coca-Cola Amatil Ltd was sold down for a second day on Tuesday, ending down 75 cents at A$12.19 as investors and analysts took at closer look at the softdrink bottler's latest financial statement.
The stock has fallen A$1.47, or 10.8 percent, from its close on Friday before the release of its full year results, and is almost one third below its closing high of A$18.00 last October.
Analysts said the company was sold off as the market looked more closely at the results, which showed a 2.5 percent rise in annual net profit to A$142.1 million.
"Underneath it all, it was a pretty poor result," said one analyst, who declined to be identified.
However, several said they were surprised at the sell-off and did not believe it reflected the long-term growth prospects for C-C Amatil, which is 36 percent owned by The Coca-Cola Co.
Analysts contacted by Reuters pointed to a fall in the tax rate, a decline in second half earnings per share and the booking of proceeds of a legal payout as prompting concern.
The tax rate fell from 32 percent in the second half last year to 17 percent in the same period this year.
"The tax rate was much lower than expected and that saved about A$21 million on last year," said one.
The lower tax rate reflected overseas development incentives offered by east European countries as C-C Amatil entered their markets, analysts said.
Earnings per share fell 12 percent for the year to 27.4 cents per share, following a share placement, but declined 22 percent in the second half to 15.7 cents per share, one analyst noted.
There was also concern about A$22 million C-C Amatil received in settlement of a seven-year old court case with Lion Nathan Ltd.
C-C Amatil booked A$6.9 million after tax from interest on the payment as interest income in its accounts.
A C-C Amatil spokesman said this followed accounting principles as the sum related to an adjustment of a purchase price, rather than the closure of a business.
